5a-architecture-00.title: The run-parameter half of StudySetup uses two incompatible conventions (named projections vs raw config types), so train_inner re-inflates TrainingConfig field-by-field out of the god-struct

retiredOverlaps.justification: distinct claim anchored in a file a file-scoped retired item also cites; NOT a re-raise

5a-architecture-00.survivingClaim: Delta over CD-005: of the seven setter-wall members, `StudySetup::set_budget` (setup/accessors.rs:62-65) is the only one with zero call sites anywhere in the repository at the pin AND the only one that is `pub` and ungated without a caller justifying the ungating (its three test-only siblings at accessors.rs:69-90 are `#[cfg(any(test, feature = "test-support"))]`-gated; `set_start_iteration` and `set_warm_start_basis_cache` are ungated because the CLI/Python resume paths call them); it writes `cut_management.budget` behind both the `StudyParams::from_config` budget-below-forward-passes validation (setup/params.rs:287-295) and the broadcast that carries `budget` to every rank (cobre-cli/src/commands/broadcast.rs:113, :215), so any use is unvalidated and rank-local. The structural halves of the title - two incompatible storage conventions, and `train_inner`'s field-by-field re-inflation - do not survive.
5a-architecture-00.argument: The two-conventions half does not survive. `.claude/architecture-rules.md:95-112` states ONE decision rule with two mechanisms: literal reuse when the config type owns only plain data with no runtime handle and no per-invocation value, a `*Params` projection when 1-3 such fields must be dropped; the table names `SimulationConfig`/`CutManagementConfig` as literal reuse and `LoopParams`/`EventParams` as projections. The code at the pin matches that rule rather than diverging from it: `LoopConfig` (config.rs:81-104) owns `n_fwd_threads`, which arrives as `train`'s per-call `n_threads`; `EventConfig` (config.rs:177-192) owns `Sender<TrainingEvent>` (:180), `Arc<AtomicBool>` (:186) and the deferred `checkpoint_interval`, none of which can sit on a struct whose module doc pins it to be holdable across a GIL release (setup/mod.rs:1-10, 120-124); `SimulationConfig` (simulation/config.rs:29-44) and `CutManagementConfig` (config.rs:136-151) own only plain data. Two mechanisms driven by different inputs under one stated rule is not two incompatible conventions. The re-inflation half is likewise explained by ownership, not by a missing type: `train` takes `config: TrainingConfig` BY VALUE (training/training.rs:328-330) while `train_inner` holds only `&mut self` (setup/orchestration.rs:109-141), so it cannot move the stored sub-configs out and must assemble a fresh value; and the `LoopConfig` arm could not be produced by a `From<&LoopParams>` impl in any case, because `n_fwd_threads` is the per-call argument and `LoopParams` carries a `seed` field (config.rs:53) for which `LoopConfig` has no counterpart at all, read post-construction by cobre-cli/src/commands/run/outputs.rs:75 and cobre-python/src/run.rs:548-549 for the output metadata. So `LoopParams` is a run-params carrier, not a strict projection, and a by-type projection cannot mechanically replace the struct literal. The only genuinely mechanical residue inside that literal is `warm_start_cuts: 0` (orchestration.rs:136) against a stored copy that is itself pinned to 0 at construction (setup/mod.rs:785-791), and the candidate's own fixShape hands that field to a sibling candidate, so it is not this candidate's residue. What does survive is the fourth anchor. `set_budget` (setup/accessors.rs:62-65) has exactly one occurrence in the whole repository outside plans/ - its own declaration, plus the prose listing at `.claude/architecture-rules.md:117`; it has no caller in src, tests, examples, cobre-cli or cobre-python. It is also the only ungated member of that group: `set_risk_measures`, `set_scheduler` and `set_hardest_first_claim_order` (accessors.rs:69-90) each carry `#[cfg(any(test, feature = "test-support"))]`, while `set_start_iteration` and `set_warm_start_basis_cache` are ungated BECAUSE the CLI and Python resume paths call them (cobre-cli/src/commands/run/policy.rs:157, :227; cobre-python/src/run.rs:1180, :1292). Two present-tense facts make the caller-free mutator worse than merely unused: `budget` is fully resolved from config through `StudyParams::from_config` (setup/params.rs:280, :330 into setup/mod.rs:439, :787), which emits the budget-below-forward-passes warning at params.rs:287-295 that a post-construction write silently bypasses; and the CLI carries `budget` to every rank over the broadcast params (cobre-cli/src/commands/broadcast.rs:113, :215; run/setup.rs:447), so a post-construction override is rank-local by construction. Note the candidate's own count is slightly off - `train_inner` performs 6 `self.loop_params.*` reads (orchestration.rs:124-130), not 7 - which does not change the verdict. No section of `.claude/rules/sddp.md` is engaged: the surviving residue touches neither the append-only cut pool, the mirrored min/max outflow rows, column-bound state pinning, `apply_nested_cvar_ub`, the NCS lower-bound patch, nor the two basis-reconstruct entry points; `contractWatch` is null on this input. Byte-neutrality is asserted for the surviving residue because the method has no call site: `cut_management.budget` continues to arrive only from config, so no LP operand, bound, row or column, no summation order and no opening order changes, leaving the parity goldens, the permute rank-invariance harness and `mpiexec -n 1` against `-n 2` byte-identical. Alignment is `neutral` rather than the filed `advances-0a`: consolidating the setup/config projection onto one engine-tagged carrier is the dismissed structural half, which the live CD-005 entry already carries at that hint; a single caller-free mutator is a pure local cleanup, and no part of it makes cobre-sddp name a sibling engine, place engine dispatch below L4, or create a single-consumer abstraction.
_needsHuman: Owner call: `set_budget` is enumerated in the declared accessor surface at `.claude/architecture-rules.md:117`, so the disposition of a caller-free ungated mutator is either remove it and edit that rules line, or keep it as a deliberate public-library knob and route it through the same validation `StudyParams::from_config` applies - the station cannot pick without the owner.

5a-architecture-01.title: The MPI wire config is not a superset-projection of StudyParams: one field is computed on params then dropped and re-read from Config, and two run-mode fields exist only on the wire
5a-architecture-01.survivingClaim: Verified delta over CD-004: the two projections are NOT independent Config readers -- BroadcastConfig::from_config calls StudyParams::from_config at broadcast.rs:144 and every wire field except training_enabled, policy_mode and the two scenario sources traces to that single params value -- so CD-004's silent MPI-vs-local value-divergence surface reduces to exactly ONE site, export_states at broadcast.rs:214, which re-reads config.exports.states although params.rs:339 already resolved it onto the params still in scope, and which cobre-python/src/run.rs:997 reads off the carrier instead. The title's structural half does not survive: training_enabled and policy_mode are front-end orchestration facts that reach no StudyParams and no StudySetup on any path, and scalar_parameters is not a Config projection, so there is no two-way symmetric difference in the Config projection itself.
5a-architecture-01.argument: Class (2) is real and verified at the pin. setup/params.rs:339 resolves export_states: config.exports.states onto the carrier, and broadcast.rs:214 re-reads config.exports.states rather than the params value that is still in scope (params is only partially moved -- policy_path at :208, boundary at :223 -- so the Copy bool at params.export_states is readable there). The asymmetry is sharpened by the third front end: cobre-python/src/run.rs:994-997 builds StudyParams::from_config and its comment states outright that export_states is captured by from_config, so the carrier is the intended single owner of that fact and the CLI wire assembly is the one site that bypasses it. The candidate's own reading of the coupling is the load-bearing delta and it holds: broadcast.rs:144 calls StudyParams::from_config, so these are not independent readers. Census corrected at the pin: BroadcastConfig has 24 fields and 24 initializers (not 26); 17 are direct copies off params, 2 more (stopping_rules, stopping_mode) are the postcard flattening of params.stopping_rule_set at broadcast.rs:155-197, 2 are scenario-source derivations from Config helpers, 2 are the run-mode reads, 1 is the duplicate export_states read. Class (3) does NOT survive as a projection gap. training_enabled and policy_mode (broadcast.rs:107-108) are pulled straight back off the wire at setup.rs:365-366, returned as separate LoadBroadcastResult fields (setup.rs:157-158) and consumed only by the front end's phase decision at run/mod.rs:166-167; build_study_setup at setup.rs:435-456 reconstructs the full StudyParams without them, git grep finds training_enabled nowhere in cobre-sddp, and PolicyMode appears in cobre-sddp only in tests/simulation_integration.rs:47,442 -- never in library src. Giving that pair a home on StudyParams, as the candidate's step 2 asks, would therefore add two fields to an L3 engine carrier with zero engine consumers, which is rule 9(c) territory; I strip it instead of confirming it, and the roadmap-consistent alternative is to leave run-mode facts on the front-end carrier (LoadBroadcastResult) and record the permitted wire divergences in the wire type's rustdoc. The local-only side of the claimed symmetric difference is weaker still: stopping_rule_set is a representation substitution forced by StoppingRule deriving no serde (the mirror types at broadcast.rs:24-51), and scalar_parameters is not a Config projection at all (params.rs:340-341 says it is loaded from disk artifacts) and rides its own broadcast_value hop at setup.rs:322, as the candidate concedes. No contractWatch was supplied and none of the station traps is touched: the narrowed fix changes no cut-pool ordering, no outflow row pair, no state-pinning bound, no CVaR nesting, no NCS patch and neither basis-reconstruct entry point. Byte-neutral: the surviving fix substitutes one read of an identically-resolved bool for another, so every operand, summation order and rendered LP byte is unchanged, and export_states only gates archive allocation (setup/orchestration.rs:143, training/session/mod.rs:262-299), which is capacity, not an observable LP value.

5a-architecture-02.title: scalar_parameters is a caller-patched placeholder rather than a constructor input, so both validate paths build stage templates against an empty parameter table and silently resolve every parameterized coefficient to 0.0
5a-architecture-02.survivingClaim: Narrowed to a missed error class, not a corrupted report: because StudySetup::new and new_with_boundary_requirements take no artifact argument, they cannot satisfy the patch protocol StudyParams::scalar_parameters' own rustdoc mandates, so the two validate paths run build_resolved_parameters on an empty table whenever config.policy.boundary is configured, and validate's documented exit-0 contract is therefore broken for exactly the three ResolvedParametersError variants cobre_io::validation::scalar_parameters does not duplicate (MissingSeason, PerStageBlockCoverage, MissingSpecificProductivity), with is_block_varying returning false on a miss collapsing a PerStageBlock row set silently and with no assert. Conceded from the candidate: no boundary-reconciliation fact validate reports reads ResolvedParameters, so nothing validate prints is wrong; the setup is built and discarded; and the validate.rs:234 mirrors-the-run-path comment concerns boundary-requirement ordering, not the parameter table, so it is not falsified.
5a-architecture-02.argument: The mechanism holds at the pin, so the candidate survives, but three of its legs do not. params.rs:174-177 documents the patch protocol and params.rs:341 writes Vec::new(); setup/mod.rs:342-344 shows new_with_boundary_requirements patching only params.boundary, and setup/mod.rs:280-282 shows new delegating straight to it, so neither constructor can fill the table because neither takes a CaseArtifacts argument. setup/mod.rs:540 threads that table into build_energy_and_templates, which calls build_resolved_parameters at setup/mod.rs:971; entries.rs:1377 and layout.rs:1045 then read every CoefficientRef::Parameter through ResolvedParameters::get, which returns 0.0 behind a debug_assert (resolved_parameters.rs:151-158). cobre-io resolves the at-name sigil against the loaded list and errors on unknown (validation/schema.rs:545, constraints/generic.rs:1044), so every id reaching get in that build is a legitimately declared id absent from an empty table, exactly as the candidate reads. First narrowing: the empty table is reached only when config.policy.boundary is configured. validate.rs run_boundary_check returns Ok(None) otherwise and cobre-python io.rs:305 guards identically, so a case with no boundary policy never constructs a StudySetup at all. Second narrowing: no fact validate reports is corrupted. reconcile_boundary reads only fcf.state_dimension, build_terminal_entity_manifest, build_terminal_fixed_post_horizon_windows, stage_templates.cost_scale_factor and boundary_requirements().inflow_lag_depth(); accessors.rs:142-190 derives the first three from the state layout, the thermal anticipated config and the initial-condition dates, none of which touch ResolvedParameters, and cost_scale_factor is patched from config, so the zeroed templates are built and discarded. Third narrowing: the comment at validate.rs:234 says only that boundary requirements are resolved before the layout is built, so it is not falsified; the text that IS falsified is the module-level exit-0 contract at validate.rs:12-26. What survives is a missed error class. cobre_io::validation::scalar_parameters already duplicates two of the five ResolvedParametersError variants (Check A covers UnknownHydro, Check B covers PerStageLengthMismatch, Check C covers duplicate id and name), so validate loses exactly MissingSeason, PerStageBlockCoverage and MissingSpecificProductivity: cases that exit 0 under validate and fail cobre run during setup. A second divergence carries no assert at all, since is_block_varying (resolved_parameters.rs:187-194) returns false on a miss, so a PerStageBlock-parameterized constraint collapses to one stage-level row in the validate build (layout.rs:1023-1031) where run builds the per-block set. The get rustdoc's own justification does not hold up either: it claims the 0.0 mirrors an LP-build-site sentinel, but entries.rs:1377 and fold_endpoint at layout.rs:1058-1068 consume the return with no fallback of their own, so no second sentinel exists to mirror. No test pairs constraints/generic_parameters.json with policy.boundary, which is why the debug_assert never fires in CI, and the integration harness at tests/common/mod.rs:154-179 documents the same protocol burden by re-parsing the whole case to patch the table rather than using either config constructor. No contractWatch was supplied and no section of .claude/rules/sddp.md governs this construction protocol: none of the listed traps is touched, and the resolved-values-freeze-at-construction invariance in the resolved_parameters module doc still holds under either leg, since neither mutates parameter values across iterations. relatedTo CD-004 decides the alignment hint: scalar_parameters is a field on the very Config-to-construction carrier CD-004 names, filled by neither projection, so making it a constructor input consolidates the setup projection rather than adding a seam. Byte-neutrality: asserted, because the run paths already patch the table (cobre-cli run/setup.rs:376 and cobre-python run.rs:996) and cobre-io rejects an unknown at-name reference, so the miss path is unreachable on every path that renders a golden; both legs of the fix therefore leave the parity goldens in tests/parity.rs and tests/common/parity_hash.rs, the rank-invariance harness in tests/common/permute.rs, and mpiexec -n 1 versus -n 2 with the same operands in the same summation order, no reassociation and no observable capacity change. The only output that moves is the validate verdict on a deck carrying generic parameters, which no golden covers today, so it needs a new regression case rather than a rebaseline.
_needsHuman: Whether the fail-loud leg changes the public surface of ResolvedParameters::get (a fallible signature or a panic) or is instead enforced as a construction-time check at the LP-build site, leaving get infallible: get is pub and must_use, so the choice is an owner call on public API shape, not a correctness question.

5a-architecture-03.title: CutManagementConfig::warm_start_cuts is a public field with a capacity contract in its doc, hard-coded to 0 at both production construction sites and read by no production consumer
5a-architecture-03.survivingClaim: `CutManagementConfig::warm_start_cuts` (config.rs:148) is the struct's only field with no production reader -- its four siblings are read at training/backward_pass_state.rs:164-165 and training/session/mod.rs:262/1042/1215 -- and its rustdoc contract 'contributes to cut-pool capacity' (config.rs:147) is false at the baseline because capacity is derived solely from the per-pool counts consumed by `pool_capacity` (cut/fcf.rs:498) and `CutPool::new_with_warm_start` (cut/pool.rs:893-895). Conceded from the title's framing: no wrong-shape defect is established for this field (that argument belongs to the distinct cobre-io manifest symbol `ProducerBlock::warm_start_cuts`), and the residue does not decide delete-versus-give-it-a-reader, because the field is `pub` on a re-exported type so removal is a breaking API change.
5a-architecture-03.argument: The inertness claim holds at the pin and the single production consumer of the struct proves it by construction: `BackwardPassInputs::from_session_fields` takes `cut_mgmt: &CutManagementConfig` (training/backward_pass_state.rs:143) and reads exactly two of its fields, `risk_measures` and `cut_activity_tolerance` (:164-165); `cut_selection` is read at training/session/mod.rs:262 and :1042 and `budget` at :1215; `warm_start_cuts` is read at no production line in the workspace, the only read being the assertion inside the `#[cfg(test)]` module at config.rs:304. Every production write stores the literal 0 -- the `Default` impl at config.rs:160, the setup projection at setup/mod.rs:789, and the `train_inner` struct literal at setup/orchestration.rs:136 -- so no caller path can make the value non-zero without going through the public field, and `config` is re-exported (lib.rs:28, `pub use config::TrainingConfig` at :102), so the field is reachable API that silently does nothing. The rustdoc line at config.rs:147, 'contributes to cut-pool capacity', is therefore false at the baseline: capacity has one owner, the per-pool count, computed by `pool_capacity(warm_start_count, max_iterations, visit_bound)` at cut/fcf.rs:498 from the `warm_start_counts` slice validated against `pool_state_dimensions` at cut/fcf.rs:151-158 and from `sr.cuts.len()` inside `CutPool::new_with_warm_start` at cut/fcf.rs:324 and cut/pool.rs:893-895. I do NOT sustain the candidate's further step that a study-wide `u32` is the wrong SHAPE for this field: that argument is borrowed from a different symbol, the cobre-io manifest field `ProducerBlock::warm_start_cuts` (cobre-io/src/output/policy/records.rs:454-459) whose 'supersedes for per-pool accuracy' note describes the manifest scalar written at policy/orchestration.rs:322, and a field with no consumer has no shape obligation to violate. The reserved-config rule does not cover this field -- it has no cobre-io input section, no `JsonSchema` derive and no schema surface; the grep over crates/ shows no loader or validator touching it -- and it names none of the five ratified seams, so no `sanctionedBy` applies. No pinned contract is implicated: capacity and slot ownership do not move under either fix direction, so `Cut pool is append-only; basis matches by slot identity` is untouched, as `warm_start_count` remains the pool's own field (cut/pool.rs:93,160-163) and the slot formula at cut/pool.rs:10 keeps its operands. Layering: removing a field from an existing engine-local config struct names no sibling engine, places no dispatch below L4, and creates no single-consumer abstraction, so the residue is a local cleanup even though the owner may prefer to land it with the config-projection candidate.
_needsHuman: Owner must choose between removing `CutManagementConfig::warm_start_cuts` (a breaking change to a re-exported public type) and giving it a real reader plus a reserved-seams entry; the verdict establishes the field is inert and its doc line false, not which of the two lands.

5b-architecture-00.title: fill_anticipated_columns re-opens the latched commitment slot at the RAW delivery-axis residue that its two sibling residue owners' own rustdoc calls the forbidden, wrong-but-compiling alternative
contractWatch: The ring axis: the delivery axis with the fixed post-horizon window excised
In-LP anticipated ring: definition-row sign, hold carry & asymmetric masking
State pinning uses column bounds, not equality rows
5b-architecture-00.survivingClaim: Narrowed to a LATENT single-site contract violation with a named precondition: fill_anticipated_columns (columns.rs:618) is the only one of four ring-residue owners that keys the deposit slot off the raw delivery axis instead of PointResolution::ring_index, contradicting both its own rustdoc at columns.rs:573-575 and the pinned deposit clause; the two residues diverge only for a plant whose fixed post-horizon width g is not a multiple of k_max AND which also holds a class-3 carried in-study decision above that window, in which case the latched slot stays frozen from fill_anticipated_slot_columns and the commitment is forced to zero (infeasible once min_generation_mw exceeds zero). Such a deck is accepted by cobre-io (thermal.rs:112/:117/:149 exempt a horizon-exceeding lead that reaches post-study), but NO shipped deck declares it - d55 is the only post-study example and resolves g equal to zero - so the defect is latent at the pin, no parity golden is wrong today, and the residue is the one-site routing change plus the missing excised-window column test, not the new shared walker the fixShape proposes.
5b-architecture-00.argument: Confirmed at the pin, with three over-reaches stripped. The divergence is exactly as filed: columns.rs:618 computes the deposit slot as `delivery_stage % layout.k_max`, eleven lines after `point` is bound at columns.rs:607, while THREE other owners of the same residue all route the physical delivery target through the ring axis first: entries.rs:159 and :166 take `point.ring_index(delivery_stage)` for the deposit row; layout.rs:718 and :724 walk the ring axis `r = stage_idx + depth + 1` and resolve `m = point.physical_target(r)` per plant; and state_space.rs:571-594 `commitment_hold_in_study_offset` applies `point.ring_index(m)` behind a debug_assert. That last one is the authority columns.rs:573-575 names in its OWN rustdoc, which states the slot as `ring_index(delivery_stage) mod k_max` - so the function contradicts its own doc, not merely its siblings'. lead_time/mod.rs:499-508 shows the two axes coincide exactly when the fixed post-horizon width `g` is zero, so a live divergence needs `g` not a multiple of `k_max`. The consequence chain holds end to end: layout.rs:728-729 masks a plant's own deposit slot (`is_interior = !is_deposit && point.is_ready_at(m, stage_idx)`), columns.rs:147-155 then freezes every masked slot to a 0-to-0 range via `freeze_masked_columns`, and columns.rs:51 orders `fill_anticipated_columns` AFTER that freeze as the sole re-open, so a wrong residue leaves the latched slot frozen and the deposit row (slot-out minus decision column equals zero) drives the carried commitment to zero, infeasible once min_generation_mw exceeds zero; nothing structural catches it, and the only two anticipated column tests (columns.rs:3613 and :3862) use g-equals-zero fixtures while entries.rs:3303 and layout/tests.rs:2030 and :2065 both carry excised-window regressions. First over-reach stripped - reachability is settled by the loader, not by an owner: cobre-io/src/validation/semantic/thermal.rs:112, :117 and :149 exempt a lead exceeding the study horizon whenever `reaches_post_study` holds, and thermal.rs:2389-2406 pins the very shape (four study stages, a three-wide fixed prefix, an in-study-decided carried tail) as a supported classification, so a deck that reaches this IS accepted upstream; the attacker's open question is answered and needs no human. Second over-reach stripped - no golden moves: only examples/deterministic/d55-post-study-anticipated-lanes ships a post_study_stages.json in the whole tree, its single post-study stage against lead_time_hours 1000 over six monthly stages resolves decider index six to Some(5), a class-3 carried delivery with g equal to zero, and none of the five parity goldens (D06, D15, D30, D34, D41) declares a post-study axis at all, so ring_index is the identity on every golden and the corrected expression yields the identical integer; the fixShape's claim that a golden must be regenerated is false at the pin. 5b-architecture-01.title: Pin-round-trip exactness for the four state families is handled by three unrelated per-family mechanisms in three modules, and the commitment family's two mechanisms never cross-reference each other
5b-architecture-01.contractCited: Delivered commitments reconcile against solver drift; exactness is unreachable
5b-architecture-01.argument: The delta this candidate adds over CD-074 is that the commitment family's two exactness mechanisms are mutually unaware and their coupling unstated; both halves are false at the pin. The reconciler's module doc (crates/cobre-sddp/src/lp/builder/commitment_reconcile.rs:8-12) names `apply_commitment_hold_col_scale_unscale` by symbol and states the relationship in the contract's own terms: unscaling removes the ring carry drift but not the deposit row drift the basis factorization introduces, so the reconciler is permanent and not redundant. COMMITMENT_DRIFT_ABS's doc (same file, :31-34) names `col_scale` as the divisor its absolute floor must survive, so the constant does cite the scaling domain. The named single owner of the pair sits outside both modules: the pinned contract at .claude/rules/sddp.md:2233-2278 states that exactness is unreachable by construction, records deleting the reconciliation on the premise that unscaling makes it redundant as a forbidden alternative that HAS shipped, and its Read line lists lp/builder/scaling.rs (`apply_commitment_hold_col_scale_unscale`) beside commitment_reconcile.rs and training/stage_solve_prep.rs, pinned by two named regression tests. The asserted load-bearing coupling is also mechanically mis-stated: the override writes only commit_out chained with commit_in (scaling.rs:132-139) while fill_bound_relaxations reads col_scale[gen_col] on thermal generation columns (commitment_reconcile.rs:194, :211-216) and divides the relaxed bound by that scale; the two touch disjoint column sets, and COMMITMENT_DRIFT_ABS exists precisely because the generation column's scale is NOT unit, which is the opposite of the premise that the tolerances are meaningful only under unit column scaling. The fixShape as filed would weaken that contract rather than single-source it: reducing the scaling.rs prose (:108-121) to a pointer strips the retained-and-why statement whose deletion premise the contract names as a shipped regression, and inverts the ownership the contract fixes, since the reconciler does not own a col_scale = 1.0 precondition. The proposed new test already exists on both sides of the coupling: scaling.rs:533 asserts the override forces exactly the commit_out and commit_in indices to 1.0 while leaving every other index byte-identical to its seed, and patch.rs:896 (fill_col_state_patches_anticipated_state_unscaled_is_exact) pins the consumer side, writing the raw commitment with no division under a unit hold scale against a non-unit scale elsewhere in the same array. 5a-performance-00.title: The opening-order chain builder recomputes a whole-tour cost sum for every candidate 2-opt reversal, and fills a symmetric distance matrix twice
5a-performance-00.survivingClaim: Only the symmetric-matrix half of the title survives as a bit-exact free win: `l2_distance_matrix` (noise_key.rs:223-243) evaluates every off-diagonal pair's L2 twice and computes the zero diagonal, and mirroring plus a skipped diagonal leaves every entry bit-identical. The whole-tour `tour_cost` recomputation in `two_opt_improve` (174-191) is real but is demoted from removable redundancy to a semantics-changing perf-sweep item, because the full sum is what keeps the accept test at 182 and the cross-start winner at 212 functions of the tours and the matrix alone, and because a path reversal changes only ONE edge at `j == n_o - 1`. The per-start `nearest_neighbor_tour` buffer allocations (141-142) do not survive at all: they are once-per-study-setup work outside the hot-path allocation ban.
5a-performance-00.argument: All six anchors resolve at the pin and the mechanism is present as filed. `two_opt_improve` (noise_key.rs:174-191) reverses `tour[i..=j]` then calls `tour_cost` (132-134), a full `windows(2)` pass over the whole tour, once per candidate reversal, inside the quadratic (i, j) sweep, inside `while improved`; `shortest_chain_path` (198-219) repeats that whole improvement from every one of `n_o` nearest-neighbour starts; `apply_chain_order` (254-266) runs it once per stage carrying three or more openings. So a whole-array scan sits in the innermost position of a triple loop, which is a real redundant-pass mechanism and grows with openings-per-stage rather than being a fixed once-per-run constant. Two of the three sub-claims do NOT survive, which is where I narrow. First, the whole-tour recomputation is not removable redundancy but the canonical full-sum accept test the function is documented to be: the doc at 138-139 pins each nearest-neighbour choice to `total_cmp` so it stays a deterministic function of `distances` alone, and 195-197 pins every comparison in `shortest_chain_path` to `total_cmp`; recomputing the full sum keeps `*cost` exactly equal to `tour_cost(tour, ...)` after every accepted reversal, so both the accept test at 182 and the cross-start winner comparison at 212 are functions of the tours and the matrix alone, never of the accumulation history a running delta would introduce. A delta reformulation is therefore a semantics change, not a free win: it flips marginal reversals and moves the winning permutation. The pinned contract heading `Backward opening order is warm-start-only` (.claude/rules/sddp.md:502-531) is both why that is permitted and why it is not free: order is warm-start-only and every outcome is written and aggregated by canonical omega, so a moved permutation cannot break declaration-order invariance or run-to-run reproducibility, but the same section states that changing the order changes the warm-start chain each opening solves from and therefore re-checks the golden parity baselines instead of assuming byte-identity. The candidate's own prescription is also imprecise on the code: for a PATH rather than a cycle, reversing `tour[i..=j]` changes at most two edges and exactly ONE when `j == n_o - 1`, so the filed two-matrix-read delta is wrong at the tail, which is further reason to hold that half back rather than confirm it as a free win. Second, the per-start allocation half does not survive: `nearest_neighbor_tour` allocates `Vec::with_capacity(n_o)` and `vec![false; n_o]` at 141-142 per start, but the sole production reach is `build_noise_key_table` called once from `StudySetup::from_broadcast_params` (setup/mod.rs:419, 467), i.e. once per study construction per rank, and the workspace hard rule bans allocation on hot paths, which this is not; per the setup-time carve-out these small per-stage allocations are acceptable exactly as written. What does survive is the symmetric-fill half: `l2_distance_matrix` (223-243) runs `for j in 0..n_o` for every `i`, so each unordered pair's L2 is evaluated twice and the zero diagonal is evaluated as well, and mirroring is bit-exact because negation is exact in IEEE-754 so `(a - b) * (a - b)` and `(b - a) * (b - a)` are the same f64, the per-pair accumulation walks the same canonical `[..n_hydros]` prefix in the same order with no reassociation, and `sqrt` is a single correctly-rounded operation; every `distances` entry keeps its bit pattern, so every downstream `tour_cost`, every `total_cmp` and the winning permutation are unchanged. Per rule 11 this is setup-time work and I quote no number: the item should still enter the perf sweep at layout 4t, because the surviving mechanism is asymptotic in openings-per-stage and not a once-per-run constant, but the sweep must treat the symmetric fill and the delta reformulation as two separately queued items with different risk.

Frequency: resolve_variable_ref has one production caller, fill_generic_constraint_entries at lp/builder/entries.rs:1363; that function is reached only from lp/builder/template.rs:419 inside build_stage_templates, whose sole production caller is build_energy_and_templates at setup/mod.rs:983, itself called exactly once from the StudySetup constructor at setup/mod.rs:535. Deliberateness: two rationale comments inside the resolver itself state the cost model for this path, at generic_constraints.rs:631-632 and 709-710, both saying a linear scan is fine because this is the cold template-build path and an O(1) reverse map is not warranted, and both contrasting with resolve_anticipated_decision at 813-826, which does carry the O(1) map because its geometry warrants it. The same path pays for the opposite discipline where cost actually scales: lp/builder/layout.rs:1921-1926 pins resolver_geom as BORROWED precisely because fill_generic_constraint_entries builds one per stage and owning would clone every range family. The surrounding code therefore discriminates by cost rather than allocating out of inattention. Title over-reach: the claim that EVERY term allocates is false. Twenty-two arms return an empty vector or unwrap_or_default (generic_constraints.rs:387, 474, 507, 533, 565, 568, 630, 639, 645, 662, 698, 709, 776, 802, 819, 824, 851, 856, 912, 915, 918, 941), and an empty Vec in Rust carries zero capacity and performs no heap allocation, so every stub-entity, absent-id and out-of-range resolution is already allocation-free. Magnitude: the loop walks layout.generic_constraint_rows, built only from declared generic constraints (entry.constraint_idx indexes ctx.generic_constraints at entries.rs:1347), so a study that declares none pays nothing at all, and where they are declared the count is proportional to the declared constraint text rather than to any whole-array scan per stage. Fix-shape hazard: the arms compose by value. resolve_hydro_outflow at 653-676 calls resolve_turbine_cells and then pushes the spillage column onto the vector it received, and the constant-productivity arm of resolve_hydro_generation delegates the same way. A single caller-owned buffer cleared per term, as filed, would move the clearing discipline out of one obvious owner and into an implicit inner-versus-outer contract spread across roughly a dozen helpers, where the inner delegate must not clear what the outer arm has already appended. Per-helper ownership of its own vector is what makes that nesting locally checkable at the baseline. No pinned contract is implicated either way: the resolver reads the layout and the position maps and hands pairs to col_entries, touching no cut pool, no Benders row and no state pin, and the input carries no contractWatch heading. Perf sweep: this item should NOT take a sweep slot. The sweep measures a per-solve deck at layout 4t, and this allocation is fully retired during StudySetup before any solve is issued, so no sweep configuration can observe it.

perfQueue.mechanism: allocation per call: one short-lived heap vector per resolved generic-constraint term per stage, returned by value and dropped after the immediately following consuming loop
